group: HOWN — How and Why in Nature
examples: What happens if you plant a seed upside down?

explain.say: However a seed lands, its root turns to grow down and its shoot turns to grow up. Plants can feel gravity, and this is called gravitropism.

explain.say: In the root cap at the very tip, some cells hold heavy grains of starch. Like sand in a jar, the grains settle on the lowest side of each cell, telling the root which way is down.

explain.say: The root then sends the growth hormone auxin to its lower side. In roots, lots of auxin slows growth down, so the lower side grows less than the upper side.

faq.q: How does a root sense gravity?
faq.a: Cells in the root cap contain dense starch grains called statoliths. They sink to the bottom of each cell, and the cell senses where they rest, a bit like flakes settling in a snow globe.
Growing down takes roots into the soil, where they find water and minerals and hold the plant firmly in place.
asks: Why do roots go into the ground?

faq.q: Why do shoots grow up while roots grow down?
faq.a: Both gather auxin on their lower side, but their cells respond differently. In shoots auxin makes cells grow faster, so the shoot curves up; in roots it slows them, so the root curves down.
asks: How do shoots know which way is up?

faq.q: What happens to plants in space?
faq.a: Without gravity, roots and shoots grow in mixed directions, steered mostly by light and water. Astronauts have grown plants on the International Space Station to study this.

faq.q: What does the root cap do?
faq.a: The root cap is a protective cap on the root tip. It shields the growing tip as it pushes through soil, makes a slippery slime, and holds the gravity-sensing cells.
asks: What is the tip of a root called?

facts: The gravity-sensing starch grains in root caps are called statoliths.
When the root cap is removed, a root keeps growing but stops turning downwards until a new cap forms.
Plants have been grown on the International Space Station to study how they grow without gravity.

quiz.why: Auxin gathers on the lower side, where it slows growth, so the root curves downward.
